capabilities: protect folders with password-based AES-256-GCM encryption
lock and unlock folders from the ribbon, context menu or commands
issue and use a one-time recovery key
auto-lock folders on idle or quit (Pro)
replace locked file names with random names (Pro)
disambiguation: Not a vault-wide or app lock by default; it encrypts one folder at a time, and notes at the vault root cannot be protected.
extras: Freemium: free tier covers one folder; Pro ($5 one-time via Lemon Squeezy) adds unlimited folders, whole-vault locking, auto-lock, hidden file names and per-folder passwords. Free never touches the network; Pro contacts Lemon Squeezy for license activation and daily checks, working offline for up to 30 days. All encryption is local, no telemetry. README carries detailed limits and sync-related warnings (locked files stay plain on disk while unlocked; backups and sync history can retain unencrypted copies).
problem: Obsidian keeps notes as plain Markdown files, so anyone or anything with disk access can read private content even when Obsidian is closed.
summary: Folder-encryption plugin that password-locks notes and attachments on disk with AES-256-GCM and unlocks them with a password or recovery key.
